title: Working on a HD-2D Idle RPG with desktop mode, inspired by Ragnarok Online
author: thetinytrex
selftext:
Like so many others that fell in love with Ragnarok Online (probably have seen like 5 projects here mentioning it), I wanted to capture some of that charm but in a format that I could enjoy without grinding for hours. So I came up with a post-apocalyptic HD-2D idle rpg game called Scraplands that can play in the bottom of your PC and be freely resized to fit your screen. I've been working on Scraplands for a few months and I even built a full idle game for mobile but "scrapped" it when I saw how good the newer Claude models were and decided to redo it all. The game has 8 different characters with different roles. You take a party of 3 out into the Scraplands and venture further and further out, getting stronger and crafting your build. Characters have bonds with not only the MC but also each other and will gain synergy skills if they fight together a lot. There's gear, boss battles, some base upgrading, skill trees, and 10+ zones.   
  
I've come to really love the world I've been building and the characters too. I think it is turning out quite nicely and am happy with it so far. I don't have any plans to release it since this was just a personal hobby. In terms of what's remaining, I'm building more city hubs, lots more enemies, and working on character dialogue and bond stories.

As for the workflow, the sprites were made in PixelLab and the environments are built by Opus 5.5 in Godot. Music from Suno. Just thought I'd share and hope someone else vibes with it.

replies.body: Thank you! That means a lot to me

comments.author: Kooker321
comments.body:
This looks incredible! I'm working on a game with a similar art style, also using Pixel Lab and Opus 5.5 (different genre).

I'd love to hear more about your workflow and how you got such high quality art, animations, and backgrounds.

replies.author: thetinytrex
replies.body:
Thank you! That sounds cool. Hope to see it. For the character sprites, I generated the characters in Illustrious on my local machine then I sent them to ChatGPT to get chibi versions with a rough reference. After that, I cutout the chibi characters and loaded them into PixelLab's Create Characters tool. I specifically used the Pro setting that let me set a color palette from lospec and upload a ref image (the chibi chat gpt image of just the 1 character). It gave me a solid sprite but I specifically was interested in one direction, South-East / South-West. I cleaned up this character direction until it was pixel perfect and with all the color adhering to the lospec palette. From there, I created new PixelLab states and animations for each character. It's a bit tedious but hardly any work compared with drawing it all by hand. I think the color palette feature is critical for making the game look cohesive and distinctive from generic games.

For the artwork, I also converted the Illustrious images in PixelLab with Image --> Pixel Art. I did two different passes. one for full body, and one for headshots so I could get good clean portraits for each character. Then using the PixelLab inpainting tool, I also created character expressions for each character.

For the backgrounds and environments, that was all Opus 5.5. I went through multiple iterations until I got right lighting, effects, props, etc. Just a lot of back and forth. I usually give Opus references to concept art found online or real locations for the vibe I'm looking for. One of the zones in my game, Quarry's End, I specifically referenced the Grand Canyon and gave reference images. I had to do a few iterations so the horizon looked good.

https://i.redd.it/jap8sxrqx11i1.png

replies.author: Kooker321
replies.body:
Wow, I'm impressed! That's far more involved then simply having Claude create the art on your behalf with the PixelLab API. And I think the results are way better than mine. 

Do you think image generation with Illustrious and ChatGPT makes a big difference vs generating the images directly in Pixel Lab?

I've been using Gemini a bit for image generation but haven't been too impressed, and haven't use it for my PixelLab workflow, just for a separate 3D project.

replies.author: thetinytrex
replies.body: I'm sure Claude + PixelLab works fine if you're okay with the style it outputs, but I don't think it will give you good animations without some manual clean-up, I need to recreate most animations or heavily touch them up by deleting or recoloring pixels, redrawing frames, or deleting frames to make the animations smooth. I think having a reference image to feed PixelLab helps quite a bit. If you generated the images in PixelLab directly without any references, then it's a bit of a wildcard what art style your game will have. I haven't toyed with the PixelLab API yet so maybe it's totally doable but I would establish some characters/sprites that you are happy with and use those as the reference for all other assets in the game.
